claims.statement: The system has three bounded layers — Layer 2 the harness/presentation shell, Layer 1 the mod package, Layer 0 the deterministic kernel, sandbox and store — and the only downward channel is Layer 1 emitting a self-contained `HarnessAction` that Layer 0 executes inline.

Because the mod ships a brief plus a submit command as plain data in `meta.summary`, any coding-agent host can drive the harness at whatever tier it supports; nothing in the mod hard-codes a specific dispatcher.

The adapter contract is asserted, not merely documented: a dispatch whose prompt lacks the line-anchored `Mandatory references:` and `Submit:` lines is reported as `[ADAPTER CONTRACT]` and the job is not spawned.

The two anchors must be line-start prefixes rather than substring tests, because `job.description` is multi-line prose in which the literal words `Mandatory references:` can occur — an `includes` check would be trivially bypassed.
Every dispatched brief must be persisted byte-for-byte at `artifacts/<rN>-<stage>-brief.md`; a refusal surfaces as `[BRIEF REFUSED]` in the receipt and counts toward `degraded`.

A brief closes with a resume-handover section so the next executor — possibly another harness or context window — knows why the previous one stopped; the equivalent of `resume` is the artifact plus its gate evidence.
